criteria.bounded_cascade: Begin from the flat staged rule and add other-model hook reentry for staged writes, keeping static cycle errors and a runtime depth bound while the triggering CRUD path remains closed to reentry. Because no current draft target carries hooks, every one of the 44 hook bodies behaves exactly as under flat staging today; the reentry machinery is pure option value for unobserved future composition. Price: cascade sequencing, bound value, interaction semantics, spanning attribution, interleaving tests and cascade-wide atomicity proof all enter the specified surface and the bounded-work budget immediately, while debuggability pays from day one as any staged write may silently recruit foreign hooks with veto power over the user's transaction — the highest cost among the four for a capability no workflow has requested.
criteria.committed_handlers: Shrink hooks to adjust-or-reject and push all 36 secondary-effect bodies into committed handlers with independent fencing and no retroactive rejection. This buys the cheapest checker (a static creation/write/schedule ban in hook bodies) and the smallest transaction shape at the highest migration price: every secondary-effect hook is rewritten and re-proven, trigger-plus-children atomicity is abandoned so partial success becomes a first-class outcome, completeness depends on retry/recovery machinery with no current dispatch evidence, and each workflow is split across two transactions that must be re-demonstrated together. The drafts' co-located, co-guarded staging is treated as having no weight, though no finding shows it unsafe.
criteria.declared_allowlist: Buy flat-rule staging at a metered price: only contract-declared parented children and pending-bound timers stage in-transaction, everything else reroutes to committed handlers. The staged set stays auditable from hook signatures, CanCheck needs no edits, and the fence/rollback/conflict story matches the flat rule over a smaller surface. Price: designing, versioning and teaching the declaration form; recurring boundary adjudication as each new hook tests the parented definition; dual-mechanism diagnostics; and a boundary drawn on syntax that neither tracks danger (parented payloads can harm; cross-row writes can be benign) nor resists gaming through re-parenting — with growth pressure toward the flat rule as soon as one legitimate cross-row staging need appears.
criteria.staged_flat: Keep every secondary write where the drafts put it: hooks stage other-row and timer effects that commit atomically with the trigger in one owner transaction, with re-run invariants, per-write versions, fenced staged targets, single ordered evaluation and no hook reentry. Migration cost is zero — all 44 bodies, including CanCheck's parented children and timers, stand unedited — and audit reads one transaction instead of a trigger plus later handlers. Price: the transaction and its rechecks must fit the bounded-work budget; staged-set atomicity is specified ahead of its engine proof; failures attribute across the trigger/staged line; and the coupling objection stands — an ambitious staged write can fail an otherwise simple user operation, so fan-out bounds remain an open follow-up rather than a settled limit.

hook_rule.instructions: For the secondary-hook-write gate, which rule best preserves the five accepted workflows (pending adjustment with version fencing, staged children/timers or an adopted replacement, revision invalidation, atomic rollback, hook negatives), keeps genuinely unsafe hook behavior failing, and minimizes migration churn and semantic risk? Judge every option under the same workflow-preservation and minimal-intervention constraints.

state: Cost and churn frame this gate: 44 CRUD hooks in 16 .can files (20 create, 23 update, 1 delete) carry the decision, 36 with secondary effects (17 parented children, 10 timers, 8 cross-row, 7 other, no deletes) against 8 settled-only bodies, and each alternative prices those bodies differently — from zero edits to full remodeling with per-site re-proof. The shared settled core costs nothing further: DESIGN pre-commit adjust-or-reject hooks, no added client parameters, no triggering-CRUD callbacks, one hook per model/operation, cycle errors, version-1 creation rows, v+1 reservations, no parent advancement from child writes. The five CanCheck workflows set the preservation bar regardless of price: pending adjustment under v/v+1 fencing, parented Transition/Notice children, Deadline timer handling, conflict-on-concurrent-change, and all-or-nothing commit with the recursive-CRUD, pending-delete, delete-adjust and snapshot-mutation negatives still failing. Priced uncertainties: T30 typing landed while R27's server-owned update/hook split awaits a T18 rule that does not exist; T28-A containment is adopted but T29 imported atomicity and split diagnostics are owed; T16 plus state-side T17a are done while durable evidence stays plan-not-proof and restarts unclaimed; example evidence is one discriminating plus one control input with none of 26 blocks on hook scenarios and R29 open; secrets carry an R17 fencing residual. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation result.
